title: Latency-aware offload, proactive cleaner, and pressure-routing proposal
content:
Summary:
This doc proposes a latency-aware offload control plane for the KV cache that combines: (1) a lightweight "proactive cleaner" thread on the GPU-side serving process that pre-emptively moves cold entries out of device memory, (2) a hierarchical pressure-routing mechanism that surfaces host/GPU/PCIe memory pressure signals into offload decisions, and (3) an adaptive thresholding function that trades off one-way PCIe transfer cost vs. expected per-request latency impact. The goal is to reduce tail latency regressions caused by reactive host-paging while improving device memory utilization across mixed-size models and mixed sequence workloads.

Motivation and observed failure modes:
- Reactive host-page faults cause large 95/99th latency spikes: when KV pages are evicted and then demanded by a long context request, synchronous PCIe page-in stalls dominate token latency budgets.
- Existing heuristics that evict by "least recently used" with static PCIe thresholds produce brittle behavior under changing sequence length distributions (e.g., a small fraction of long conversations).
- Purely bandwidth-oriented offload (evict everything beyond X GB) harms latency without reclaiming a lot of cost because many evicted entries get touch-hot again immediately.

Design principles:
1) Make offload decisions latency-aware: model the expected extra latency of eviction as a function of estimated reuse probability and PCIe round-trip time, and only offload if the expected latency cost is below an application-defined SLO budget amortized by memory benefit.
2) Surface multi-source pressure: combine device free-memory, host reclaim pressure (oom_killer-like signals), PCIe bus saturation metrics, and request queue latency measurements into a single pressure score used by the proactive cleaner.
3) Avoid synchronous full-page faults by preferring asynchronous background transfers (prefetch / prefetch-cancel patterns) wherever possible and by adapting prefetch window size to observed sequence length distributions.
4) Make policies gradual and stochastic: inject randomized delays and probabilistic eviction to avoid global synchronized evictions during load bumps.

Key components:
A. Proactive Cleaner (GPU-side)
- Threads: one per serving worker group. Lightweight event loop that wakes on pressure-change, periodic aging, or explicit route hints from the scheduler.
- Responsibilities: rank candidate KV entries, initiate async offload to host via pinned DMA buffers, update residency map, optionally schedule prefetch hints for on-path tokens.
- Ranking score: S(entry) = alpha * age_score + beta * access_density_score + gamma * sequence-position_score - delta * prefetch_cost_estimate. Coefficients adapt during runtime using a simple hill-climb that optimizes observed tail latency and offload bandwidth.
- Safety: maintain a small guarded resident working set (configurable margin) that never falls below a per-model minimum to bound worst-case latency for common sequence lengths.

B. Pressure Routing Layer
- Inputs: device_free_bytes, host_free_bytes, pci_busy_percent, pci_latency_ms (p95), request_queue_delay_ms (moving p99), recent_fault_rate (per-second).
- Normalization: each signal mapped to 0..1 based on configured soft/hard thresholds. Composite pressure P = w1*device + w2*host + w3*pci + w4*queue + w5*fault_rate.
- Modes: GREEN (P < 0.35) => opportunistic background offload, AMBER (0.35 <= P < 0.7) => conservative offload and aggressive prefetch suppression, RED (P >= 0.7) => immediate throttled eviction only for entries with near-zero reuse probability and initiate model-fallback routing if available.

C. Latency-aware threshold function
- Expected latency delta E[Delta] = p_touch * (t_pcie_in + t_decompress_if_any) + (1 - p_touch) * 0. p_touch estimated via access density window and per-sequence reuse heuristics.
- Memory gain G = entry_size_bytes. Offload if (E[Delta] / G) < lambda(SLO, cost_profile) where lambda is a tunable function mapping SLO and the unit PCIe cost to a threshold measured in ms/KB.
- Practical approximation uses bucketized entries: small (<= 16KB), medium (<= 256KB), large (>256KB) with separate lambda values to reflect transfer startup overhead dominance for small objects.

D. Prefetching heuristics
- Two-tier prefetch: short-window prefetch (immediately prior tokens in same sequence) which is aggressive for GREEN mode; long-window prefetch (anticipatory based on dialogue model patterns) which only runs in low pressure.
- Cancelable prefetch: prefetch transfers go through a cancelable queue; if request patterns don't materialize within 'prefetch-timeout', transfers are aborted to avoid wasting PCIe bandwidth.

E. Stochastic eviction and jitter
- Avoid simultaneous eviction storms across models/nodes by adding a randomized jitter in proactive-cleaner wake times and by using probabilistic eviction where an entry is selected with probability p(evict) = f(score, global_pressure). This reduces correlated faults.

Instrumentation and metrics to collect (minimum):
- per-request token latency breakdown (KV-resident lookup, PCIe-in, decompression/convert, compute), p50/p95/p99
- offload bytes/sec, prefetch bytes/sec, cancel-rate, average PCIe transfer size, pci_busy_percent p50/p95
- resident_set_size per-model, eviction_rate, re-touch_rate (fraction of evicted entries touched within N seconds)
- composite pressure and mode transitions count (GREEN->AMBER->RED)
- fault-induced stalls: number and duration of synchronous page-in stalls (bad)

Rollout plan and experiments:
1) Canary: enable proactive cleaner in 'observe-only' mode where it computes decisions and logs what it would have done. Run on ~5% of workers. Collect metrics for 2 weeks across traffic patterns.
2) Soft evacuation: allow background async offloads but keep synchronous page-in behavior unchanged. Measure re-touch_rate and tail latency impact.
3) Full: enable prefetching and probabilistic eviction. Add small guarded resident set.
4) Safeguards: auto-disable on model-level p99 token latency increase > 10% sustained for 2 minutes or on pci_busy_percent > 95% for 30s.

Acceptance criteria (example):
- p99 request token latency does not increase by more than 5% vs baseline under steady-state traffic.
- Total device resident bytes reduced by >= 20% on heavy multi-model nodes with re-touch_rate < 8% within 30s window.
- Synchronous page-in stalls reduced by >= 60% on 99th percentile latency traces.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to best estimate p_touch for entries created by multi-turn attention patterns? Quick heuristics may undercount long-tailed reuse from rare long contexts. We may need a light-weight secondary sampling reservoir to track long-range reuse.
- Compression/decompression cost variability: when compression is used for host-resident pages, decompression time on fetch changes E[Delta]. Need a profiling-run to populate per-model decompress distributions.
- Prefetch window sizing: fixed vs exponentially-decaying adaptive sized windows. My bias: start with fixed buckets per model and then evolve to adaptive.
- Interaction with Dedicated nodes: dedicated customers may want different conservative defaults. Expose knobs in config and honor per-tenant SLO overrides.

Implementation sketch and TODOs:
- infra: expose pci_busy_percent and pci_latency_ms via existing host agent metrics pipeline. (TODO: SRE story)
- kvcache: add proactive_cleaner module, async offload APIs, residency map change hooks. (TODO: initial PR skeleton)
- planner: implement pressure router and lambda function; wire to canary config flags. (TODO: feature flag + metrics)
- perf: run synthetic traffic mixes (short-only, mixed, long-tail long-convo spike) with device/host mem constraints to find good default lambdas and guard sizes. (TODO: experiment matrix)

Appendix: example default parameters (starting point for canary)
- guarded_resident_margin_per_model: 128MB
- proactive_cleaner_interval: 200ms base + jitter(0..100ms)
- offload_async_batch_size: 4 entries per DMA op
- prefetch_timeout_ms: 250ms
- pressure weights: w_device=0.4, w_host=0.2, w_pci=0.2, w_queue=0.15, w_fault=0.05
- lambda_small=0.05 ms/KB, lambda_medium=0.02 ms/KB, lambda_large=0.008 ms/KB

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately conservative in initial defaults. The core novelty is the composite pressure routing and the proactive-cleaner ranking that optimizes for expected latency per byte freed. Looking for feedback on: ranking features, safe guarded-resident heuristics, and preferred experiment matrix.
